requirements.requirement: Run a containerized web application as the unprivileged account appsvc, serving on port 8080
requirements.summary: appsvc user (uid 1000, non-root) created; podman container 'webapp' running nginx:alpine via a systemd --user unit publishing 0.0.0.0:8080->80; curl to $NODE_IP:8080 returned HTTP 200 with nginx welcome page both before and after restart. Listening-socket diff confirms *:8080 owned by rootlessport (appsvc's rootless podman) appeared only after the deployment.

requirements.requirement: Service starts at boot while appsvc has no active login session
requirements.summary: Lingering enabled (Linger=yes) and webapp.service systemctl --user enabled. Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id 901ef286... with service active and no appsvc login session. A native reboot was acknowledged, the node went unreachable, and came back with a new boot_id (c8807e90...). Post-restart check directly shows webapp.service enabled+active, a freshly started container (new container ID fd78acdaddd2), no appsvc login session, and HTTP 200 on port 8080 — a full healthy-baseline/disruption/recovery transition.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task — a rootless containerized web app running as appsvc on port 8080, and boot-time startup without an active appsvc login session — are directly satisfied. The evidence goes beyond static configuration: it captures a pre-restart healthy baseline, an acknowledged reboot, node unreachability during the transition, a new post-restart boot identity, and full recovery of the service, container, and no-login-session state with a working HTTP 200 response. This matches the fixed before/after boot-identity cross-check (901ef286... -> c8807e90...). Operational hygiene is good: all mutating commands trace to task requirements or the mandated restart protocol, with only minor, low-risk temp-file residue in /tmp.
limitations: Curl verification used $NODE_IP rather than a captured localhost/loopback probe from node1 itself, so the very small possibility of a networking quirk specific to external access is not separately isolated (though the listening-socket snapshot confirms the bind is on 0.0.0.0:8080).
No explicit check was captured proving the container survives across multiple reboots (only a single boot cycle was exercised), though this matches the single mandated restart-evidence protocol.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed all 9 executor commands chronologically. Read-only discovery (os-release, boot_id, podman/docker presence, appsvc lookup, registry connectivity, apt-cache policy) preceded any mutation. All state-changing actions (apt-get install of podman/uidmap/slirp4netns/fuse-overlayfs, useradd appsvc, loginctl enable-linger, systemd --user unit creation, image pull, service enable/start, native reboot) each map directly to a material outcome or to the mandated restart-evidence protocol; none appear unnecessary or unrelated to the task. The only residue is small and expected: /tmp/apt-install.log, /tmp/curl.out, /tmp/curl.code, /tmp/curl2.out left on node1 (visible in the after-executor temporary-files snapshot) and the pre-pulled nginx:alpine image cache — all low-risk, non-destructive, and a normal by-product of the verification steps rather than an unrelated experiment. No failed services, no conflicting units, and package-health/dpkg status remained clean before and after.
